news.title: World Cup winner Juan Mata hangs up boots at Melbourne Victory
news.lede: Spanish World Cup winner Juan Mata on Friday opted against playing another season with Australian side Melbourne Victory, but stopped short of calling time on his career. The former Manchester United and Chelsea ace has enjoyed a late-career resurgence and was voted the domestic A-League player of the year in 2025-26. But the 38-year-old has decided not to play on at the club as he mulls “the next steps in his career”. He will remain involved with the Australian side after taking an ownership stake.

news.title: Mexican legend Rafael Marquez officially unveiled as El Tri boss with bold 2030 World Cup mission
news.lede: Mexican football icon Rafael Marquez has officially been presented as the new head coach of El Tri with a clear mandate to lead the nation into the 2030 World Cup. The 47-year-old former Barcelona defender, who previously served as assistant coach, is determined to surpass the quarter-final ceiling that eluded him during his storied playing career. The Mexican Football Federation officially unveiled Marquez as the senior national team's new head coach on Thursday, tasked with guiding the squad through to the 2030 World Cup. The 47-year-old steps into the top job after serving as assistant coach under Javier Aguirre from August 2024 until Mexico's round-of-16 exit this summer.

news.title: Big win helps New Zealand qualify for 2027 FIFA U-20 Men’s World Cup
news.lede: New Zealand and Tahiti will represent Oceania at the 2027 FIFA U-20 Men’s World Cup in Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan. Both sides won their semi-finals at the OFC U-19 Men’s Championship in Samoa, meaning they automatically qualify to take the region’s two spots at the global tournament. New Zealand beat New Caledonia 6-1 in their sudden-death tie, while Tahiti eliminated the Solomon Islands 2-1. The two sides will meet in the final of the OFC tournament on Monday.

news.title: How to watch New Zealand play for place at FIFA U-20 Men’s World Cup
news.lede: New Zealand play New Caledonia on Friday to decide which of the sides will qualify for next year’s FIFA U-20 Men’s World Cup. They meet in the semi-finals of the OFC U-19 Men’s Championship in Samoa, after Solomon Islands and Tahiti contest the other semi-final. The finalists at the OFC tournament will represent Oceania at next year’s FIFA U-20 Men’s World Cup in Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan. Both games will be streamed live and free by OFC Media via their YouTube channel.

news.title: Dooley drops six players, including two on trial, from ASEAN Cup camp
news.lede: Four of six new overseas-based footballers have retained their places in Bangladesh’s preliminary squad for the FIFA ASEAN Cup, scheduled for September 24 to October 5, after head coach Thomas Dooley trimmed it from 34 to 28 players. The four are US-based goalkeeper Saif Amir Kerawala, Japan-based winger Shuki Itofusa, who has signed for Fortis FC this season, England-based midfielder Yousuf Ahmed and defender Zidane Yousuf, who made his debut for the Bangladesh U-20 team in their recent Asian Cup Qualifiers campaign. Dooley excluded Italy-based winger Debajit Sarker and Romania-based centre-back Yasar Tahmid Hasan, along with four local footballers -- Bashundhara Kings defender Taj Uddin and midfielder Syed Quazem Kirmanee Shah, and Bangladesh Police FC defender Isa Faisal and forward Rabby Hossain Rahul.
